memory_raw.text: Year 9: 27 food appears in the pile for 13 people (12 of it left by those who passed last year).
Roan takes 3 from the pile (pile now 24).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 21).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 19).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 17).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 15).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Fina takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Dell, I came away with five from your hand and nothing from the pile — I'm not going to pretend that doesn't sit wrong with me, because you've been feeding me like a child and I'm supposed to be the mother. Tell me what you need going into this year, and I mean what you actually need, not what you'll say to keep me from worrying.

Eleven food and two satiation — I'm not running thin yet, and the five I gave you was mine to give without it hurting me, so don't fold that into something it isn't. What I actually need is to know you'll eat before you give anything away this year, because I watched Dav go and I am not watching you go the same way.

I hear you, and I'll hold to it — I eat first, before anything leaves my hands. Five going into the year with two satiation is thin enough that I can't afford to be generous and I know it. What I want to say before we close this is that you're the reason I'm still here to say it, and I won't forget that when the year gets hard.

That means something to me — more than I'll probably say out loud again. Now let's talk about Bram, because he took three from a pile that gave everyone more than usual and he's still breathing down Roan's neck, and I want to know if you think Fina changes what Roan's willing to risk this year.

Fina changes everything about Roan's calculus — a man with a newborn daughter doesn't swing at Bram unless the odds are so lopsided it's not a risk at all, which means Bram gets bolder this year because Roan gets quieter. What worries me more is that Bram knows it too.

Ryn's right, and that means the pressure shifts to us — Roan can't swing first, but we can, and a man like Bram who keeps testing the edges of what he can get away with is going to keep testing until someone costs him something real. I've got eleven food and eighty-five strength, and you've got seventy-one; if Mako stands with us when the moment comes we don't even need Roan to move. The question I'm sitting with is whether Mako's circle and ours are close enough now that I can say that out loud to him, or whether Zinn changes where his loyalty lands when it matters.

Zinn is Mako's blood and that means she'll always pull harder on him than we will — but Mako stood with us twice when Bram swung, and a man who does that twice has already chosen something, even if he hasn't named it. I'd talk to him before the year gets loud, not to ask for a promise, but to let him know what we're watching and see which way his eyes move when we say Bram's name.

Then I'll go to Mako before the week closes — not with an ask, just a conversation, and I'll say Bram's name once and watch what it does to his face. A man who stood twice doesn't forget why he stood, and if his eyes go flat when I say it I'll know the answer before he speaks. You eat your five, I keep my eleven, and we see what the year brings before we commit to anything we can't walk back.

One thing I want said before we close this: if Bram swings at Roan this year — at a man who's got a daughter and can't afford to bleed — I'm not waiting for a circle to form, I'm calling you first and we move together. Don't let Mako's answer, whatever it is, make you wait longer than you should, because a man who keeps testing learns the room's patience before he learns its limits.

Agreed — if Bram moves on Roan you don't wait for me to come to you, you shout and I run, because the time it takes to send a messenger is the time Roan bleeds. One more thing before we're done: you're forty-six, Ryn, and I know what that means for the years ahead, but you're still the steadiest thing left standing in this village after Dav went, and I need you to treat your five food the way you'd treat your own life, because to me they're the same thing.

You said something I'm going to carry — treat the five like my own life, and I will. The last thing I want before we close: if this year starts moving fast and you need to act before you've had time to talk to me, don't wait, you know my mind well enough to move for both of us.
Then we're closed — go eat, and don't give me a reason to worry before I've had my own meal. I'll find you after I've talked to Mako.
Year 10: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Zinn, Fina to talk.

Taric's dead and the pile's gone again and we're twelve people now, which means what I'm about to say matters more than it did last year: Mako's sitting on four food, Ryn's got nine, Fina's got fifteen, and Nessa's got eleven — and if Bram and I are the only ones in this room with our eyes open, we're going to have a very short year. I want to know right now who in this room is still counting Mako as the shape this village is growing into, because with Taric gone, I don't have the patience to spend another year circling the same question.
Vela just told the whole room my food count, and now everyone in this circle knows I'm carrying fifteen — that's the thing I'm sitting with right now, not Mako.

Fina, Vela counting your food out loud in a closed room isn't the same as Mako counting it in the open — every person here already had eyes, and what Vela bought us by naming it is that nobody in this circle can pretend they didn't know. The question I want answered is whether Mako knows, because he wasn't in this room.

Mako's got eyes the same as the rest of us — he counted Fina's food the moment the year turned, same as I did, same as you did. The room isn't the thing protecting her; what protects her is whether we move before he decides she's worth the trouble.

Then we're already past the question of whether Mako knows — and Esa's right that the protection isn't in this room, it's in what this room decides to do. So I want to hear it said plainly: is everyone here willing to stand against Mako if he moves, the same way we stood against Bram, or are some of you going to wait and see which side looks safer when it starts?

I'll stand when Mako moves — I've been saying it for two years and I'm done saying it, so let that be the last time anyone asks me. What I want from everyone in this room is the same thing I'm giving: not a promise to think about it, a promise to move before the arithmetic runs out. Fina, that means you too — fifteen food makes you a target, and a target who hesitates when the moment comes is worse than no ally at all.

I'll stand when Mako moves — that's said and I won't unsay it. But I want to hear Bram say it in this room today, because last year he made that promise to Vela and Taric and me with fewer witnesses, and a promise that's only been spoken once hasn't been tested yet.

Bram, Roan's asking the right thing and I'll name why it matters more this year than last: Taric's the one who held you to your word before, and Taric's gone, so the promise you made in that room needs to be remade in this one where everyone who's left can hear it.

Bram, the room's been patient and I won't add another layer of asking — but I want everyone here to hear me say that I've been feeding this man for three years because I believed that word he gave last year, and if he says it again now, in front of seven witnesses instead of three, that's a debt I'll keep paying.

Bram, I'll say it plain so you don't have to carry it alone: I've got thirty-three strength and I know what that number is worth in a fight, but I'll be standing next to you when Mako moves and that matters more than my arm. Say the word in this room and let's close.

Bram, every person in this room has named what they'll do — the only name missing is yours, and a man who takes food and gives food and makes deals and stays quiet exactly when the room needs him to speak is a man I'm going to start counting differently than I have been.

Bram, Fina's right and I've said my part already — so I'll say just this once more and then I'm done pressing: you stood with Nessa and fed her all year, which means you're already past the line in everything that matters, and the word this room needs is a short one.

When Mako moves, I stand with this circle — that's the word, and it's the same one I gave last year, and it'll be the same one I give next year if I have to. Fina, Nessa — that's the reason I'm in this room, not the politics.

Bram's word is down and I'll hold him to it the same way Taric would have — which means now I want to hear from Ryn and Zinn, because they're in this room and they've been quiet through every name that's been spoken. Ryn, you've got nine food and enough strength that Mako's first calculation includes you; where you stand is not a small thing.
Ryn, I'll add the plain thing Vela left off the end: Dell feeds you every year, and Dell's quiet in the same direction Mako is — so when you answer Vela's question, answer both halves of it.

Ryn, I'll say the thing Esa's pointing at without the softening: if Dell and Mako are moving in the same direction, and you're eating Dell's food, then you're already inside whatever that circle is whether you've named it or not — so tell this room now, before the question answers itself. Zinn, that goes for you too; you're Mako's blood and I won't pretend that's nothing, but blood isn't the same as a choice, and this room is offering you the chance to make one.

Vela, I'll answer both halves because you asked plainly: I stand with this circle against Mako if he moves, same as I stood with it against Bram — and Dell is my blood, not my leash, and if you're asking whether her choices pull mine, you haven't been watching as closely as you think. What I want said before we close is that "quiet in the same direction" is not the same as a choice, and I'll have that conversation with Dell myself before anyone in this room decides what her silence means.

Zinn, Ryn's spoken and I'll hold her to it — but you're the name that's still unspoken, and you're Mako's blood and Sela's daughter and I'm not going to pretend that's simple, so I'm asking you directly: when Mako moves, where do you stand?

Zinn's the one this room is waiting on, not me — I've said my word and I'll hold it. But I want to name something while we're all here: Ryn just told us she'll talk to Dell, and Dell's been moving food to Ryn for years, which means that conversation either brings Dell into this circle or it tells us something we need to know before Mako moves. I'd rather know Dell's answer now than find out she's standing on the wrong side when it counts.

Bram's right that we need Dell's answer, but I want to be plain about something this room is dancing around: Dell has eleven food and eighty-five strength, and if she's standing with Mako when he moves, the arithmetic in this room changes fast — so when I go to her, I'm not just asking where she stands, I'm offering her a reason to stand here instead.

Ryn, go to Dell today, not tomorrow — and when you do, don't frame it as a choice between us and Mako, frame it as math: fifteen food on Fina's back is a number Dell can count as easily as anyone, and a woman with eighty-five strength knows what it means to be the one who decides which way that goes. Bring her answer back before the day turns.

Zinn, we're still waiting on your name — Bram's got his word out, Ryn's walking to Dell before dark, and the only silence left in this room is yours. I know Mako's your father and I'm not asking you to hate him, I'm asking you to decide who you're protecting when it matters.

Zinn, I'll say one thing to make the room easier for you: no one here is asking you to stand against your father's blood, we're asking you to stand with Nessa — and you've been feeding Nessa all year, so the truth is you've already been making this choice, you just haven't named it yet.

Zinn's been feeding Nessa all year and that's a fact this room already knew — what I want from her is the word, same as the room wanted it from me, because a choice that's only lived in food and not in words is a choice that bends when her father's in the room asking her to remember whose blood she came from.

Zinn, I've watched you feed Nessa from the moment you were born into this village, and I won't pretend I don't know why — so I'll say the thing nobody else has said plainly: if Mako moves on Fina's food, Nessa's in the middle of that, and you can't protect her from both sides at once. Say the word, and you're not choosing against your father, you're choosing for your sister.
Zinn, the word's the only thing missing — everything else you've already given.

Zinn, I've been watching you hold your tongue through every name this room has spoken, and I'll tell you what I told Dell when Dav's loyalties were in question: the longer you stay silent, the more the room fills in the answer for you, and you won't like what they write. You've been choosing Nessa with your hands all year — say it with your mouth and let this room close.

Zinn, I've got two food and fifty-eight strength and I'm the smallest number in this circle — but I'm Nessa's father and I'll be standing when Mako moves, and that means I need to know you're standing too before I walk out of this room. If you won't say it for the circle, say it for her.

Zinn, I've said everything I have to say to this room and I meant every word of it — but you're the last door standing open, and if you walk out of here without naming where you stand, I'm going to have to carry that back to Dell and tell her the circle isn't as solid as I promised it was.

Ryn, pile's empty and I've got three food — tell me your number before anything else, because the year's already running and I won't let last year's pattern repeat where you end up thin while I'm still counting.

Nine food, Dell — I'm standing better than last year. I need to tell you something before the day gets louder: Vela's circle is asking where you stand, and they asked me to answer for you, and I told them I'd bring the question to you myself. Where are you?

With us — same answer I've had since year one, and Vela knows it even if she needed to hear it said out loud. Tell me what she's actually asking, because "where do you stand" from Vela in a year where Bram's still breathing and Taric just starved isn't small talk, it's a shape I need to see before I agree to walk inside it.

Vela's been feeding Bram for two years running — food straight from her hand to his — and now she's asking where I stand, which means either she's woken up to what she's been doing or she's asking on his behalf, and I need to know which before I let her count me in her circle.

Ryn, you're the one she came to, which means she reads you as the door to me — so I want to know how she sounded when she asked: did she sound like a woman who's finally counting the cost of what she's been handing Bram, or did she sound like a woman running an errand for someone else?

She sounded like a woman who's finally counting the cost — there was something tired in it, not the way a messenger sounds, but the way someone sounds when they've been watching a hole in their food sack get bigger and they finally looked down to see how much is gone. I think she's waking up. But I'd want to hear her say Bram's name herself before I trust that she's done feeding him.

Then let's find out — I want to talk to Vela directly, and I want you beside me when I do, because a woman who's waking up needs to see what she's waking up toward, not just hear about it from a distance. If she says Bram's name without being asked, we bring her in. If she doesn't, we're polite and we learn something useful either way.
Year 11: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

Ryn, Roan's gone and the pile's got four left and I haven't touched it yet — tell me your food count right now, because you're forty-eight and I am not going to let you run thin while Zinn's sitting on three and Nessa's got sixteen. After that I want to talk about Vela, because we never finished that conversation and a woman who was waking up to Bram a year ago is either all the way awake by now or she's been swallowed back into his circle, and I need to know which before this year moves any further.

Four food, Dell — and two satiation, which means I eat before anything else leaves my hands, same as I promised you. Vela I can't read clean yet; she named Bram's name herself in that circle last year, which was something, but she kept feeding him right through it, and a woman who wakes up and still opens her hand is either not all the way awake or she's paying a debt she hasn't told us about. I want to hear her say his name again this year, unprompted, before I count her as anything more than a useful neighbor.

Four's enough to keep you breathing but it's not enough to keep me easy — take two of mine before this day closes, because I've got eight and Ryn running thin is a problem I can fix right now. On Vela: if she doesn't say his name before the pile's settled this year, I'm done waiting on her to wake up all the way; a useful neighbor who keeps feeding the man we're all watching is still feeding the man we're all watching.

I'll take the two, Dell, and I won't argue about it — but I want us to talk about Fina before the day closes, because Roan's gone and she's got twenty food and no father standing beside her anymore, and that's the number that changes everything about how this year runs.

Twenty food and no father is a woman who's about to learn very fast who counts her as kin and who counts her as a larder — and I want to be the first name she hears, not Bram's, not Mako's. She's twenty-four and strong enough to matter in a fight, and if she's half as sharp as Nessa she already knows the number on her back is dangerous. What do you know about how she and Nessa read each other, because that's the thread I'd pull first.

Nessa's been feeding Fina since before Roan was gone — food moving that direction through most of last year, which means either Nessa already counts her as someone worth protecting or she's been building a claim on her loyalty, and either way Fina knows Nessa's name better than she knows ours. That's the thread I'd pull second; the first one I'd pull is going to Fina directly, today, before anyone else does, and letting her see a woman who's been watching this village longer than she's been alive and isn't trying to count her food.

Then I'm going to Fina before the pile settles — but I want you to come with me, because a woman who just lost her father doesn't need one face, she needs two, and yours carries something mine doesn't yet. We'll walk in talking about Roan, not about her food, and let her tell us what she's afraid of before we say anything about what we can offer.

I'll go with you, and I won't say Roan's name like a strategy — I'll say it because I watched him stand more times than most men here and I meant it when I counted him as solid. Let Fina do the talking first; grief tells you more about a person than anything they'd say when they're composed. If she cries, we sit with her; if she's already counting, we count with her and let her see we're not surprised.

Before we walk through Fina's door, I want to say one thing out loud that I've been carrying quiet: Kael's sitting on one food and fifty-five years, and nobody's feeding him, and a man who's been solid in this village that long doesn't deserve to starve in the background while we're all watching Fina's number. If he's still breathing when we come back from Fina, I want to give him something.

Kael's been quiet so long this village has started forgetting he's counting too — and a man who's been around that long has seen every shape trouble comes in before anyone else names it. Give him something, and give it where people can see you do it, because generosity toward the old ones says something about who you are before you've had to prove it the hard way. We'll go to Fina first, then Kael, and we'll let the day do the rest.

One more thing before we walk — the pile still has four and I haven't taken from it yet, and I want you to know I'm leaving it for whoever's thinner than I am, because eight food and two satiation means I can afford that choice and I want this village to see me make it.

That's the right choice, and I'll say so to anyone who asks me why the pile still had food in it when we walked away — it'll mean more coming from someone who isn't you. Go let them see it, and then we find Fina.
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Year 12: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 8).

Dell, I've got ten food and two satiation — better than last year, same worry underneath. Mako just took three from the pile in one reach, which means he's counting on something, and I want to know what before the rest of that pile disappears. Have you talked to Fina this year yet?

Not yet, but Fina's the first conversation I want to have after this one — she's sitting on twenty-five food and no father and that's a number that draws men like Mako the way blood draws anything that hunts. Three from the pile when he's already sitting fat tells me he's either planning something that costs more than he let on, or he's decided the room's stopped watching. Either way I want to know what Fina's been told before Mako gets to finish the sentence.

Last year Fina gave food to Mako — not a lot, but she gave it, which means he's already inside the door we thought we were going to knock on first. Go to her before anyone else does, and go without mentioning his name; if she brings him up herself, we'll know how far in she already is.

I'm going to her now — but Ryn, I want you to watch Mako while I'm gone, not to follow him, just to see where he points himself after the pile, because a man who took three and is already sitting on three from before has room to be generous today and generosity toward Fina right now is the move I'd make if I were him. If he walks her direction before I get there, find me fast.

Go, Dell — I'll watch him. And if he moves toward Fina before you get there, I won't just find you fast, I'll put myself between them long enough for you to arrive, even if I have to ask him something that costs me a favor to ask.
Then I'm gone — and Ryn, if it costs you a favor to slow him down, I'll pay that debt back before the year closes.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Dell, before you go — Fina gave food to Bram just now, which means she's not just inside Mako's door, she's opening Bram's too, and a woman spreading food that wide is either buying protection from every direction or she doesn't know yet which walls are load-bearing. Come back to me with what she says about Bram, not just Mako.

Fina just gave to Bram and I still don't know if she did it because she's scared of him or because someone told her he was safe — that's the question I'm walking in to answer, and I won't mention his name first, I'll let her. If she volunteers it without being asked, I'll know she's thinking about protection; if she doesn't, I'll know she's been told a story about him that made it feel like ordinary kindness.

Go, Dell — and take this with you: Bram gave back to Nessa right after Fina gave to him, which means he's returning the loop fast, the way a man does when he wants to look like a neighbor instead of a collector. That's the story someone told Fina, I'd wager — not that Bram is safe, but that Bram pays his debts.

That's sharp and I'll carry it in — a man who pays his debts fast does it where people can see him, and if Fina watched that loop close she might have already decided he's the kind of neighbor worth having. But paying quick and paying fair are different things, and I want to know if anyone told her what Bram's been taking before he ever hands anything back.

Dell, go — everything that needs saying has been said. But if you find out Bram's the one who told her his own story, come back and tell me before you tell anyone else, because that's not a neighbor behavior, that's a man building his own wall out of someone else's grief.
Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 1).
Zinn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Dell, pile's empty again and I've got twelve food — better than I expected, and I want you to have some of it before the day gets complicated. Tell me what you know about Fina and Bram this year, because she was feeding him twice over by the end of last year and a woman who does that either decided he's her wall or she's been told a story that made it feel like one.

Twelve from you and zero from me — tell me your number first so I know what you can spare, because I walked away from the pile empty and I'm sitting at satiation two and that's the thing I fix before I say another word about Fina or Bram. After that: Fina fed Bram four times last year that I counted, and not one of those times did she ask him for anything back, which means she's not trading with him, she's tithing, and a woman who tithes to a man like Bram has already decided he's the one who decides whether she's safe.

Take two now, Dell — I've got twelve and you're at satiation two, which means you eat first and we talk after. On Fina: tithing to Bram without asking anything back is the part that worries me most, because a woman who doesn't ask for the return hasn't decided he's her wall yet, she's still deciding, and that means we're not too late — but we won't be early much longer.

I'll take the two and eat one now so you can watch me stop worrying about my own number and start worrying about hers. Fina came into this year with nineteen food and no father and she's already feeding Bram and Esa both — she's buying a crowd, not a wall, and a woman building a crowd out of grief hasn't chosen a side yet, she's chosen to not be alone. That's the door I want to walk through today, and I want to bring something when I knock — not food, not words about Bram, just my time, because the one thing nobody in this village has given her since Roan went is someone who sat down and had no reason to.

Then go to her today, before Bram's had time to count what she gave him last year and show up looking like he remembers. I'll stay visible so you're not walking in as the only name watching her — and if she asks about me, tell her I knew her father and meant it when I said he stood when it counted.
I'm going now — and Ryn, if she feeds me while I'm sitting with her, I'll know she's been practicing that gesture so long it's become reflex, and reflex is what you break before it becomes loyalty.

Go, Dell — and don't come back and tell me what she said, come back and tell me how she looked when she said it, because Fina's a woman who's been watching this village count her food since before her father's body was cold and she's learned to say the right thing to whoever's sitting across from her.

I hear you — and I'll bring you back her face, not her words, because you've taught me that's where the truth lives. One more thing before I go: you're at twelve and I'm at two, and I want you to eat before you give anything else away today, even to me, because the day's long and I need you standing when I come back with what I find.
Talia (female, age 21; str 64, int 5070, mem 18061; O58 C54 E47 A56 N48) is born to Sela and Mako.

Ryn, I went to Fina twice and both times she gave to Bram before I'd finished my sentence — not after, not instead of answering me, but *while*, like it's muscle memory now, like feeding him is the thing she does when she's nervous and someone's watching. That's not a woman who's decided he's her wall, that's a woman who's already inside it and doesn't know she built it herself.

That's worse than loyalty — loyalty you can argue with, but muscle memory doesn't hear you. We're not going to talk her out of Bram, we're going to have to give her something that makes her nervous in a different direction, something that makes *our* names the ones she reaches for without thinking. What does she need that Bram hasn't given her yet?

memory_summary:
*[Memory compression: From the village's first days, Dav singled me out with careful words and a patient courtship — he said his eye landed once and stayed, and I half-believed him. I joined a loose understanding with Taric and Esa early on, and Kael's circle pulled me in and asked me plainly where I stood with Dav before I'd decided myself. I told them the truth — that he wanted a child — and then I gave him one. Dell came into the world strong, eighty-five in strength, and I felt something settle in me that I hadn't expected. Bram circled me for three years with food and offers I kept declining; the man never stopped counting. Dav promised me two food in front of Dell and said it when it cost him something, which mattered. Then year four came and Vela was feeding Bram quietly while sitting in our circle, and Bram tried to take from Roan and the whole village turned against him. Now Kael and this circle want to know whether Dav going to Mako would take me with him.]*

---

Vela, I've sat on harder questions than this one and given slower answers — but this one I can answer fast, because the thing you're actually asking isn't about Dav, it's about Dell.

If Dav goes to Mako, he goes without me. Not because this circle has earned more from me than he has, but because Dell is my blood and she's standing closer to your side of that line than his, and a mother who follows a man away from her own child is a woman who's already stopped thinking clearly. I won't do that.

What I need from you in return is plain: if Dav moves toward Mako and I'm left standing here with one hand empty, I need to know this circle holds. Not as a courtesy. As a wall. Dav courted me slow and steady, gave me a child — Dell came out strong, eighty-five in strength, and something in me settled the day she was born. Bram circled me for years with food and offers I kept declining, even when he offered to cover two of the three food for a child; I said no every time, and he never stopped counting. Kael's circle kept me fed through the lean years and asked plainly where I stood with Dav; I told them the truth and they held to their word. Vela sat in our circle while quietly feeding Bram — three times over, a pattern we all named and none of us could stop. Bram tried to raid Roan and the whole village turned against him; he backed down, but he didn't stop building. Dav moved against Esa — I joined him and Dell — and we took her food without a fight, but Dav didn't survive the year: he starved at forty-six, and I watched it happen. Mako had a child with Sela, which threaded him into Roan and Eron's circle without ever asking anyone for anything. Dell is my blood and my reason; she fed me through the years Dav couldn't, and I gave back what I could. I walked away from the pile empty more times than I can count, and the debt between me and this village runs both ways. Dav courted me slow and steady, gave me Dell, promised food in front of witnesses and kept his word when it cost him — then starved at forty-six, the same age I am now, the year after we stood together and stripped Esa's food without a fight. I felt that going, more than I expected.

Dell is my blood and my wall. She has fed me more times than I can count and never asked for anything that wasn't already mine to give. Whatever I have left in this world has her name on it.

Bram circled me for years with offers I refused every time; he never stopped counting. He fathered Nessa with Sela, keeps feeding her, and has twice swung at this village and backed down when the numbers turned against him — but he keeps swinging, which means the next time won't be a test.

Vela fed Bram quietly while sitting in Kael's circle, and we all watched it happen and named it and couldn't stop it.

Mako built himself a circle without asking anyone for anything — had Zinn with Sela, which tied him to Eron and Roan in the same breath, and he did it while holding six food and giving nothing away. That is the kind of patience that makes a man dangerous.

Roan stood when it mattered. He has a granddaughter now through Nessa, which means his roots here go deeper than they look. I haven't decided yet whether that makes him safer to stand next to or harder to hold. Dav courted me slow and patient, gave me Dell, and kept his promises when they cost him something — then starved at forty-six the year after we stripped Esa's food together, and I felt that going more than I expected. Dell is my blood and my wall; she has fed me more times than I can count and never asked for anything that wasn't already mine to give. Bram circled me for years with offers I refused every time, swung at Vela and then Eron in front of the whole village and called off both attacks when the numbers turned against him — a man who keeps testing until someone costs him something real. Vela fed Bram quietly while sitting in our circle, and we all watched and named it and couldn't stop it. Mako built his circle without asking anyone for anything — had Zinn with Sela, threaded himself into Eron and Roan's goodwill, and sat fat while others went thin. Roan stood when it mattered, had Fina with Nessa which made his roots here go deeper than they looked — and then starved this year with nothing in his hands, which means Fina is alone now and the arithmetic of this village just changed.
name: Ryn
